abstract: Segment-routing traffic engineering requires rapid computation of optimal paths under dynamic demand. We present a PHP implementation that leverages the Floyd-Warshall algorithm with path reconstruction to evaluate segment-routing decisions on arbitrary directed graphs. The algorithm preserves optimal substructure and runs in $O(n^{3})$ time, where $n$ is the number of nodes. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 64-core processor (1 physical core, 2 logical threads, 7.7~GB RAM, Aether-Framework 7.0.0-1017-azure) shows a mean latency of 43 378.67 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 23 053 ops/s over 30 iterations. These results demonstrate that PHP can serve as a viable prototype language for traffic-engineering research. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/php-backend-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261116_150240_the_complexity_of_traffic_engi}
